newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Bay State again hit by weather.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Bay State again hit by weather.

text.p: Bay State Gas Co will be reporting another warm weather hit to earnings Thursday, President Joel Singer said in an interview.
He also said it is "hard to imagine" directors raising the dividend at their May 1 meeting, as they have in recent years.
"At this point," he said, Bay State's payout ratio of 77 percent -- based on the present quarterly rate of $0.385 and last year's earnings of $2 per share -- is too high.
"The solution is to raise earnings. We've just got to get earnings up," he said.
Noting the weather was warm during the company's second quarter, ended March 31, Singer said the resulting "very downward pressure on earnings (had) a significant impact."
He declined to discuss specifics, but the First Call consensus for the quarter is $1.59 per share compared to $1.75 per share in 1966's second quarter.
Neighboring Commonwealth Energy System has already reported the March quarter was 10.8 percent warmer than 1997.
In reporting a first quarter earnings decline to $0.98 from $1.07 in fiscal 1996, the utility said the six percent warmer weather cut earnings $0.12 per share.
The company said this was partly offset by the addition of 6,300 new customers during the previous year.

At that time, the company also said warm weather and EnergyUSA start up costs would pull earnings for all of fiscal 1997 below the then consensus estimate of $2 per share, excluding the sale of its 17.5 percent MASSPOWER interest.
Singer told Reuters EnergyUSA's drag on fiscal 1997 earnings is expected to be $0.07 to $0.12 per share on revenues of $40 to $50 million compared to 1996's $17 million.
Next year, however, the unit is expected to show operating profits of $0.07 to $0.12 per share on revenues of $80 to $100 million, he said.
Bay State expects to invest $1 to $2 million of capital, excluding acquisitions, in Energy USA this year and $5 to $10 million in fiscal 1998, Singer said.
He noted the unit was put together from the utility's energy products and services business segment late in fiscal 1996 and early this year.
Singer said the company now expects it "will be reporting a significant gain" on the sale of its stake in MASSPOWER, an operating cogeneration facility.
The "early feedback is the market is well in excess" of the interest's $2.4 million book value, he explained.
